/**
 * Opaque child-workspace declarations for build-system repositories.
 *
 * A local repository is inert workspace data. The package loader validates
 * its directory and workspace marker before discovery, then treats the tree
 * as an opaque boundary unless a declared input names a path inside it.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
/**
 * Schema for a workspace-relative opaque child repository declaration.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Declaration = Schema.TaggedStruct("LocalRepository", {
    path: Schema.NonEmptyString,
    branch: Schema.optional(Schema.NonEmptyString)
});
/**
 * Checks whether a value is a local repository declaration.
 *
 * @category guards
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const isDeclaration = Schema.is(Declaration);
/**
 * Declares an opaque child Smithers workspace at a workspace-relative path.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const make = (path, options = {}) => Declaration.make({ path, branch: options.branch });

/**
 * Changesets status and version operations.
 *
 * This module also declares the irreversible exec action shared by the
 * release targets that mutate external or working-tree state.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import { Action } from "@smthrs/flow";
import * as Exec from "./Exec.js";
/**
 * The irreversible variant of the shared exec action.
 *
 * It carries the same payload, result, and error as {@link Exec.Exec} but is
 * declared at the `irreversible` tier, so the engine refuses to retry it
 * blindly and no verification, replay, or cache-population path may execute
 * it. Release targets use it for every run that mutates manifests or external
 * registries.
 *
 * @category actions
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const ExecIrreversible = Action.make("smithers-build/exec-irreversible", {
    payload: Exec.Payload,
    success: Exec.Result,
    error: Exec.ExecError,
    tier: "irreversible"
});
/**
 * Implements {@link ExecIrreversible} with `node:child_process` spawn.
 *
 * It delegates to the shared confined exec runner, so environment scrubbing,
 * bounded output capture, and process-group interruption match sealed execs.
 *
 * @category layers
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const ExecIrreversibleLive = (options) => ExecIrreversible.toLayer((payload) => Exec.run(options, payload));

/**
 * Flow declarations for `.smithers/FACTORY.ts`.
 *
 * A repository's flows live under `flows/` and describe themselves in their
 * own entry files: the description, the capabilities, the model. What a flow
 * cannot say about itself is how the repository presents it: the one-line
 * `summary` a listing shows under the id, and whether it is `featured`, one
 * of the handful the repository recommends first. That prose belongs to the
 * factory declaration, under `S.Factory({ flows })`, riding the same
 * `summary` and `featured` pair every target carries.
 *
 * `Smithers.Flow` is that declaration. It is inert: it names a flow id and
 * carries its presentation, and nothing reads it until the
 * `FactoryProjection` target projects the declarations over the discovered
 * flows into the `flows` rows of `.smithers/factory.json`. A declaration
 * that names no discovered flow fails that projection by id, so a typo is
 * never silently featured.
 *
 * @since 1.0.0
 */
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
import { Declaration } from "./Flow.vibe.platform.js";
export { Declaration, Flow, idPattern, maximumIdLength } from "./Flow.vibe.platform.js";
/**
 * Reports whether a value is a flow declaration.
 *
 * @category guards
 * @since 1.0.0
 */
export const isFlowDeclaration = Schema.is(Declaration);

/**
 * The CLI verbs a generated pipeline may run across a target graph.
 *
 * A pipeline declaration names verbs, not target kinds: `smithers-build test '//...'`
 * is one command a CI job runs, the same verb-and-pattern shape Bazel's own CI
 * uses for `bazel test //...`. Before this module a PACKAGE.ts file named them
 * with bare strings, so the authoring surface was four quoted words whose
 * spelling nothing checked at the call site and whose meaning the attr name did
 * not explain.
 *
 * This module gives each verb a value. `Verb.Build`, `Verb.Test`, `Verb.Lint`,
 * `Verb.Docs`, and `Verb.Review` are declarations a PACKAGE.ts file
 * references by name, so a misspelling is an unresolved identifier rather than
 * a string the renderer rejects at plan time.
 *
 * The set is deliberately smaller than {@link Target.Kind}. `run` is
 * addressable from the CLI and is not here: run targets include development
 * servers and source-tree scaffolds, and an unattended pipeline must not start
 * or mutate one merely because it is addressable. A pipeline that runs `run`
 * targets is therefore not a declaration that exists, rather than one the
 * renderer refuses.
 *
 * `review` IS here, and it is not in {@link all}. A pipeline may declare a job
 * that runs the model reviews, and that job is the only thing that plans them:
 * the aggregate `ci` verb does not.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
/**
 * Schema for the `build` verb.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const BuildVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("build") });
/**
 * Schema for the `test` verb.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const TestVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("test") });
/**
 * Schema for the `lint` verb.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const LintVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("lint") });
/**
 * Schema for the `docs` verb.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const DocsVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("docs") });
/**
 * Schema for the `review` verb.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const ReviewVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("review") });
/**
 * Schema for the aggregate `ci` verb.
 *
 * `ci` is not a {@link Target.Kind}: it is the CLI's own name for planning every
 * kind over one pattern in a single invocation. It has a value here so a
 * pipeline declaration can ask for the aggregate without restating the four
 * verbs it stands for.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const CiVerb = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.Literal("ci") });
/**
 * Schema for one verb a generated pipeline may run.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Verb = Schema.Union([BuildVerb, TestVerb, LintVerb, DocsVerb, ReviewVerb]);
/**
 * Builds every target in the pattern.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { Smithers } from "@smthrs/targets"
 *
 * // Runs `smithers-build build '//...'`
 * export const verbs = [Smithers.Verb.Build]
 * ```
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Build = BuildVerb.make({ name: "build" });
/**
 * Runs every test target in the pattern.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Test = TestVerb.make({ name: "test" });
/**
 * Runs every lint target in the pattern.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Lint = LintVerb.make({ name: "lint" });
/**
 * Runs the documentation-parity check over the pattern.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Docs = DocsVerb.make({ name: "docs" });
/**
 * Runs the model-assisted review targets in the pattern.
 *
 * Deliberately its own verb rather than a flavour of `lint`. A review target
 * diffs the checkout against a base revision and spawns a model CLI, so it
 * needs a full-history checkout, a model binary, and a credential that no
 * ordinary lint job has. Kept under `lint` it was planned by every wildcard
 * `lint` and by the aggregate `ci`, and both died at plan time on a shallow
 * pull-request checkout where `origin/main` does not exist. A job that wants
 * the reviews asks for them by name.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Review = ReviewVerb.make({ name: "review" });
/**
 * The verbs the aggregate `ci` command runs, in the order it aggregates them.
 *
 * A pipeline declaring exactly this set is the aggregate `ci` command, so the
 * renderer collapses it to one step. {@link Review} is not here and never
 * will be: `ci` is the unattended, hermetic verb, and a model call is neither.
 *
 * @category constants
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const all = [Build, Test, Lint, Docs];
/**
 * Plans and runs every verb over one pattern in a single invocation.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { Smithers } from "@smthrs/targets"
 *
 * // Runs `smithers-build ci '//packages/...'`
 * export const verb = Smithers.Verb.Ci
 * ```
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Ci = CiVerb.make({ name: "ci" });
/**
 * Schema for one verb a generated pipeline step may run, aggregate included.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const PipelineVerb = Schema.Union([BuildVerb, TestVerb, LintVerb, DocsVerb, ReviewVerb, CiVerb]);
/**
 * Checks whether a value is a pipeline verb.
 *
 * @category guards
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const isVerb = Schema.is(Verb);
/**
 * Checks whether a value is a verb a generated pipeline step may run.
 *
 * @category guards
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const isPipelineVerb = Schema.is(PipelineVerb);
/**
 * The CLI subcommand one pipeline verb names.
 *
 * @category accessors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const command = (verb) => verb.name;
/**
 * The target kind one verb selects.
 *
 * The return type is what keeps this module and {@link Target.Kind} from
 * drifting: a verb whose name is not a kind the CLI has would not typecheck
 * here.
 *
 * @category accessors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const kind = (verb) => verb.name;

/* eslint-disable jsdoc/require-description, jsdoc/no-restricted-syntax */
/**
 * The inert placeholder a declaration carries in place of a stamp value.
 *
 * A stamp resolves after keying, so a declaration that must render a stamp
 * into a plain string (a linker flag, a Dockerfile build arg) carries this
 * token instead of a value. The token spells only the stamp's name — or, for
 * a secret-valued stamp, the environment variable's name — so it is safe in
 * key material, and the executor replaces it immediately before spawn.
 *
 * @category constructors
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const token = (name, value) => `{smthrs:stamp:${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ name, value })).toString("base64url")}}`;

/**
 * The model CLI vocabulary every target that makes a model call shares.
 *
 * The engine names live in their own module rather than in the review rule
 * that first needed them, so the rule that spawns a CLI and the rule that
 * validates an author's `engine` option read one list. Borrowing the
 * vocabulary from a neighboring rule is how the two drift: the manifest rule
 * used to refuse an unknown engine with a message naming an engine this
 * schema has never admitted.
 *
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
import * as Schema from "effect/Schema";
/**
 * The model CLI a target runs a prompt through.
 *
 * Reviews use tool-free provider requests: `claude` selects Anthropic Messages
 * and `codex` selects OpenAI Responses. The generic `promptEngine` utility
 * and explicit trusted-host executable overrides use the corresponding CLI.
 *
 * @category schemas
 * @since 0.1.0
 */
export const Engine = Schema.Literals(["claude", "codex"]);
